narrative.overview:
OpenKerf is built like a measuring instrument on a workbench, not like a creative app. It has a quiet grey chassis, one teal for actions, and numbers set in monospace with tabular figures so they can be read from a metre away without being misread. The design is the precision. The interface steps back so that three things stand out: the bed with the work on it, the machine's state, and the values that decide a burn.

The density is that of a tool you work in for hours: a 56px top bar, a 38px action bar under it, a narrow tool rail on the left, a context panel on the right, and a stage in the middle with the bed drawn to scale. Most decisions in the system were measured, usually as a contrast ratio, a pixel size or a number of layers that stay visible. The reasoning is in `frontend/src/lib/tokens.css`. That file is the only place where colours and sizes appear as values, and since its component layer it is also the only place where the shared patterns (field, label, help, card, list row, chip, badge, notice, empty state, icon, button, fold, ask row) are drawn.

There is one theme, light. The system serves two scenes with it: the desk, with a mouse, and the tablet beside the machine, possibly with gloves and in poor light. Below 1200px the type scale moves up one step, and below 1200px or on a coarse pointer every target becomes at least 44px.
keyCharacteristics: Plain and precise: hairline borders, 6px corners, flat at rest.
One accent (Coolant Teal) for actions and choices; red only for stopping and destroying.
Numbers always in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures; words in IBM Plex Sans.
The bed is the brightest surface; the stage around it is decoration.
Every shared pattern is drawn once, in `tokens.css`, and guard tests refuse a second drawing.
Touch is first-class: 44px targets and a larger type scale on tablets.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Coolant Teal means "this is an action", "this is chosen" or "the machine is working". Do not use it for headings, decoration or reported states such as "measured" or "in use"; a badge takes its colour from the state, never from the accent. The colour-for-new-work ring is in Ink because it shows a state, not an action.

rules.name: The Stop Wins Rule
rules.body: Stop Red never loses contrast, size or position to anything else. The stop button is the strongest thing in the top bar, keeps its word at every width, and sits above every dialog.

rules.name: The No Grey Lies Rule
rules.body: Grey means "nothing to report", so it is only for offline and unknown. Every other machine state has a colour, defined once in `.machinedot`. The one deliberate grey on a job is "Last known state": when the controller link is lost, the job card's phase turns Muted Ink and its bar stops, grey, because the app no longer knows.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Values Rule
rules.body: Set a label in mono only when the label is a value: a number, a coordinate, or somebody's own name (a saved jog position). Set verbs such as Unlock, Earlier or Cancel in Sans. The status bar follows the same split: X, Y and percentages in mono, the words around them in the interface face.

rules.name: The Fold Is Not A Heading Rule
rules.body: Fold lines use sentence case at weight 500 in the reading colour, with a triangle marker. Uppercase and letter-spacing are only for section labels.

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts on hover. A target that moves while you aim at it shifts under the cursor. Hover changes fill, border colour or underline thickness only.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and duration from a token in `tokens.css`, and measure the contrast before you add one. `tests/one-system.test.ts` refuses a component that reads an undefined token or writes a raw value.

Do use the shared faces as they are (`.btn`, the field well, `.field-label`, `.label-section`, `.title`, `.help`, `.link`, `.card`, `.listrow`, `.chip`, `.badge`, `Notice`, `EmptyState`, `Why`, `Icon`, `details.fold`, `.ask-actions`, `.machinedot`) and only say where they sit and how wide they are. `one-system.test.ts` and `one-button.test.ts` fail on a local redrawing.
Do set every number in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures, and format it through `Intl`.
Do give a control with its own height `min-height: max(<its own>, var(--target-min))` so it reaches 44px under 1200px or on a coarse pointer.
Do keep Stop and Pause labelled at every width.
Do pick a dialog width from `--dialog-s/m/l/xl` through the `size` prop.
Do pair every status colour with an icon or a word.
donts: Don't use Coolant Teal for headings, decoration or reported states.
Don't lift, scale or shift anything on hover or focus.
Don't fade a disabled control with opacity. Drain it to Raised Grey and Muted Ink.
Don't show any machine state other than offline or unknown in grey.
Don't let a dialog or anything else cover the stop button.
Don't run the kerf animation anywhere but the progress of a running job.
Don't put a coloured stripe on the side of a box; use a notice with its tint, edge and icon.
Don't type an icon as a glyph (×, ⋯, ›, +); draw it with `Icon.svelte`.
Don't load fonts from the network, and don't let the OS draw a checkbox or accent colour.
